knowledge:
- key_parameters: pairedSamples=Specifies whether miRNA and gene expression values derive from the same individuals (TRUE) or different cohorts (FALSE) ;; method=In performGeneDE/performMirnaDE, specifies the pipeline (edgeR, DESeq2, voom, or limma) ;; group=The name of the biological condition variable of interest ;; contrast=A string indicating the levels of the variable of interest to compare (e.g., "PTC-NTH") ;; design=An R formula specifying the linear model with the variable of interest and covariates ;; pCutoff=Statistical significance threshold for differential expression or enrichment ;; pAdjustment=Multiple testing correction method (default is "fdr") ;; database=The gene-set database to use for enrichment (e.g., "GO", "KEGG", "Reactome") ;; score=Confidence level for mirDIP predictions ("Very High", "High", "Medium", "Low") ;; includeValidated=Whether to include miRTarBase validated interactions (TRUE/FALSE) ;; test=Integration method ("correlation", "association", "fry", or "auto") ;; partial=Whether to perform partial correlation analysis to account for group effects (TRUE/FALSE) ;; associationMethod=Method for association test ("fisher", "fisher-midp", "boschloo")
- alternatives: For differential expression, edgeR (Quasi-Likelihood), DESeq2, or limma-voom can be used for RNA-Seq, while limma is used for microarrays. For functional enrichment, ORA, GSEA, or CAMERA can be selected. For target identification, mirDIP (predicted) and miRTarBase (validated) are combined. For integration, correlation is preferred for paired data, while association tests (Fisher's, Boschloo's) or rotation gene-set tests (fry) are used for unpaired data.
- when_to_use: Use this package when you have both miRNA and gene expression data (paired or unpaired) from microarrays, RNA-Seq, proteomics, or single-cell transcriptomics, and you want to identify dysregulated miRNA-target networks and their functional consequences.
- pitfalls: Simultaneous use of adjusted p-value and logFC cutoffs for differential expression is discouraged. Microarray expression matrices must be normalized and log2 transformed beforehand, whereas RNA-Seq/miRNA-Seq requires raw count matrices. Partial correlation analysis is only effective with at least 20-30 samples per condition. mirDIP database is only available for human miRNAs; other species default to miRTarBase validated interactions. Boschloo's exact test is computationally intensive compared to Fisher's exact test.

workflows.name: paired_integration_workflow
workflows.intent: Perform differential expression, functional enrichment, target retrieval, and correlation-based integration for paired miRNA and gene expression data.
input: meta (data.frame containing sample metadata with primary, mirnaCol, geneCol, and condition columns)
workflows.stages: 1. Load expression matrices and prepare metadata ;; 2. Create a MirnaExperiment object ;; 3. Visualize expression variability using MDS plots ;; 4. Perform differential expression for genes and miRNAs ;; 5. Access and visualize differential expression results ;; 6. Perform functional enrichment analysis (ORA and GSEA) ;; 7. Retrieve predicted and validated miRNA targets ;; 8. Perform correlation-based integration ;; 9. Extract and visualize integrated miRNA-target pairs
workflows.code:
library(MIRit)
data(geneCounts, package = "MIRit")
data(mirnaCounts, package = "MIRit")
meta <- data.frame(primary = colnames(mirnaCounts),
                   mirnaCol = colnames(mirnaCounts),
                   geneCol = colnames(geneCounts),
                   disease = c(rep("PTC", 8), rep("NTH", 8)),
                   patient = c(rep(paste("Sample_", seq(8), sep = ""), 2)))
experiment <- MirnaExperiment(mirnaExpr = mirnaCounts,
                              geneExpr = geneCounts,
                              samplesMetadata = meta,
                              pairedSamples = TRUE)
geneMDS <- plotDimensions(experiment,
                          assay = "genes",
                          condition = "disease",
                          title = "MDS plot for genes")
mirnaMDS <- plotDimensions(experiment,
                           assay = "microRNA",
                           condition = "disease",
                           title = "MDS plot for miRNAs")
ggpubr::ggarrange(geneMDS, mirnaMDS,
                  nrow = 1, labels = "AUTO", common.legend = TRUE)
model <- ~ disease + patient
experiment <- performGeneDE(experiment,
                            group = "disease",
                            contrast = "PTC-NTH",
                            design = model,
                            pCutoff = 0.01)
experiment <- performMirnaDE(experiment,
                             group = "disease",
                             contrast = "PTC-NTH",
                             design = model,
                             pCutoff = 0.01)
deGenes <- geneDE(experiment)
deMirnas <- mirnaDE(experiment)
geneVolcano <- plotVolcano(experiment,
                           assay = "genes",
                           title = "Gene differential expression")
mirnaVolcano <- plotVolcano(experiment,
                            assay = "microRNA",
                            title = "miRNA differential expression")
ggpubr::ggarrange(geneVolcano, mirnaVolcano,
                  nrow = 1, labels = "AUTO", common.legend = TRUE)
plotDE(experiment,
       features = c("TG", "TPO", "DIO2", "PAX8"),
       graph = "barplot", linear = FALSE)
supportedOrganisms("Reactome")
ora <- enrichGenes(experiment,
                   method = "ORA",
                   database = "GO",
                   organism = "Homo sapiens")
set.seed(1234)
gse <- enrichGenes(experiment,
                   method = "GSEA",
                   database = "KEGG",
                   organism = "Homo sapiens")
knitr::kable(enrichmentResults(gse), digits = 2, caption = "GSEA results. A table listing the affected KEGG pathways in thyroid cancer.")
enrichmentDotplot(ora$downregulated, title = "Depleted functions")
gseaPlot(gse, "Thyroid hormone synthesis", rankingMetric = TRUE)
experiment <- getTargets(experiment)
experiment <- mirnaIntegration(experiment, test = "correlation")
partial <- mirnaIntegration(experiment, test = "correlation",
                            partial = TRUE, pCutoff = 1)
integrationResults <- integration(experiment)
head(integrationResults)
cor1 <- plotCorrelation(experiment,
                        mirna = "hsa-miR-146b-5p",
                        gene = "DIO2",
                        condition = "disease")
cor2 <- plotCorrelation(experiment,
                        mirna = "hsa-miR-146b-3p",
                        gene = "PAX8",
                        condition = "disease")
ggpubr::ggarrange(cor1, cor2, nrow = 1,
                  labels = "AUTO", common.legend = TRUE)

workflows.name: unpaired_integration_workflow
workflows.intent: Perform integration analysis for unpaired miRNA and gene expression data using association tests or rotation gene-set tests.
input: experiment (a MirnaExperiment object containing differential expression results and retrieved miRNA targets)
workflows.stages: 1. Perform one-sided inverse association analysis using Fisher's exact test with mid-p correction ;; 2. Perform integrative analysis using the rotation gene-set test (fry) method
workflows.code:
exp.association <- mirnaIntegration(experiment,
                                    test = "association",
                                    associationMethod = "fisher-midp",
                                    pCutoff = 0.2,
                                    pAdjustment = "none")
exp.fry <- mirnaIntegration(experiment,
                            test = "fry",
                            pAdjustment = "none")
